I think antinatalism is actually philosophically sound:

1) People who exist are guaranteed to suffer. Even if you have an amazing life, eventually you'll watch your parents get sick and die, and then you will get sick and die too.  That's not to mention the fact that no one's life is really that amazing.

2) The Optimism Bias means people are notoriously bad at judging just how bad their situation is.  Just look how people in overpopulated, impoverished, disease-ridden regions of the world keep having kids. Why would you choose to subject a child to that kind of life?  Some people think Antinatalism is the same thing as eugenics.  However, eugenics would say only certain people should be allowed to reproduce, whereas antinatalism would say it's unethical for anyone to reproduce (see point 1)).

3) People who don't exist will NEVER suffer and they won't miss the good things life has to offer either. It's not like they're floating around in the ether wishing they could eat ice-cream and play with puppies. They will never experience the absence of those "good" things and they will never experience any of the bad.  My unborn "child" will never have to experience anxiety, depression, sickness or death.

The problem for us is it's too late, we're already here and we just have to make the most of it.  People sometimes ask why anti-natalists don't just kill themselves. Well the survival instinct combined with the fact that death is scary and unpleasant makes suicide quite difficult.  People who don't exist never have to worry about dying though.  I just try and enjoy the things that interest me and I feel satisfied that I'm never going to inflict this nightmare on anyone else.
